My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. I know this soil — it's the North China Plain, flat, deep loam, fed by groundwater wells. My father grew wheat and maize here. I do the same. It works. The grain station takes everything, the price is stable enough, and I know exactly what to do from October to October without guessing.

I have 6 mu under my name. I do wheat in winter, then maize on the same plots in summer. That's the rotation everyone here does. No tricks. I tried cotton once in my thirties — too much hand labor, my back won't take it anymore at 51. My wife still helps but we're not young. Wheat and maize I can mostly manage with the village machinery cooperative.

For wheat, I'll use 良星99 — the seed dealer in town has been pushing it for years and my neighbor's yields are good. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing and urea at jointing. I water three times: before winter freeze, at jointing, and at heading. I spray herbicide in February and do one fungicide pass before harvest.

For maize, I direct-seed right after the wheat combine leaves the field — no time to plough in summer. I use 郑单958, it's been reliable. Summer rains are usually enough but I'll run the pump once at seeding if the ground is dry. One herbicide pass, one for corn borer.

I don't overthink this. I've seen neighbors try new things and lose money. I just need steady yield to cover costs and have something left.
